steps.note: Pre-flight: orders.customer_id must still be integer NOT NULL and customer_id_new must not exist yet.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'customer_id' AND data_type = 'integer' AND is_nullable = 'NO') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not integer NOT NULL'; END IF; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'customer_id_new') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id_new already exists'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert (and on any update of customer_id).
steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $$;

steps.note: Add nullable bigint column customer_id_new (metadata only, no table rewrite) plus the sync trigger, under one brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. lock_timeout 300ms with retries, so app queries never queue behind the lock for long (the app's statement timeout is 2s).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint; CREATE TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF customer_id ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync(); RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add column'; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill ids 1..1,000,000 in 200k-row autocommitted batches. The app only inserts, so there are no row-lock conflicts. Then VACUUM without truncation (truncation would take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE) so later batches reuse the dead space.

steps.note: Backfill the rest: ids above 10,000,000 (live inserts made before the trigger existed). Rows inserted after the trigger already have the value. Then VACUUM (no truncate).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id BETWEEN 10000001 AND 10200000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 10200000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; VACUUM (TRUNCATE false) orders;

steps.note: Add NOT VALID check constraints under a brief lock, with retries: customer_id_new is NOT NULL and equals customer_id. From here on they are enforced on every new row.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq CHECK (customer_id_new = customer_id) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add check constraints'; END $$;

steps.note: Validate both constraints. This is a full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block the app's reads or inserts. The plan fails here, before anything is dropped, if any row was missed or differs.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq;

steps.note: Swap in one short transaction, with lock retries: SET NOT NULL (no scan: proven by the validated check), drop the trigger and the checks, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. Then drop the trigger function.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..120 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; DROP TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_not_null; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to swap columns'; END $$; DROP FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync();

steps.note: Verify that orders.customer_id is now bigint NOT NULL, then refresh planner statistics for the new column.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'customer_id' AND data_type = 'bigint' AND is_nullable = 'NO') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not bigint NOT NULL'; END IF; END $$; SET statement_timeout = 0; ANALYZE orders;
